context.body: Genesis through Deuteronomy distinguishes requests, responses, priestly formulas, intercession, restitution, pardon, retained consequence, and stated refusal to pardon. The bounded source is Leviticus 4:1–35.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Repeated sin-offering cases identify offender, offering, priestly atonement.
observations.label: Sin-offering cases end with “forgiven”: action

observations.body: the stated result that the person or assembly is forgiven.
observations.label: Sin-offering cases end with “forgiven”: response

payload.posture: Read Leviticus 4:1–35 as requests, law, and pardon evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The passage gives bounded Forgiveness evidence, but it does not make this request, response, condition, means, or outcome a universal procedure: Repeated sin-offering cases identify offender, offering, priestly atonement, and the stated result that the person or assembly is forgiven.
payload.title: Sin-offering cases end with “forgiven”
